findings.reason: the section exists so a pick can tell luna's cost from astra's ("prefer the lifted lane's cheaper models has no fact behind it"), and this mechanism gives all three the same figure, so the done-when ("With luna declaring rates dated within the horizon, its row's `price` holds those figures") cannot hold and the price deliverable misses its whole purpose.
findings.text: §37 sets each candidate's `price` from one `backend_rate_statuses` call "keyed by the candidate's backend", but `backend_rate_statuses` classifies only the resolved `backends` map, whose single entry per lane carries the lane's default model (verified on the live flight: `config.backends` = {claude, clive, codex, native}, `codex` carrying `gpt-6-sol`/`sol`, with no per-model entries), so a lane model's own rates — declared under `lanes.<lane>.models.<key>` — are never read and every model of a lane renders the default model's price

findings.reason: a worker cannot assert on a `backends` entry that does not exist, so the node would either fail its gate or silently weaken the assertion, and §37's stated provenance path is wrong for the same reason.
findings.text: §37 requires that "the lane expansion carries `suits` onto each derived entry" and its done-when asserts "the resolved derived entry for each codex model holds its `suits` with its provenance", but `expand_lanes` builds a per-model `backends` entry only for a `<lane>-<key>` name that some layer already declares, and §19 (landed) retires those names, so no derived entry exists per lane model

findings.reason: the done-when asserts "the backend with no model is keyed by its bare name", which fails for any backend whose dialect or local marker differs from its name, and the false "keeps its existing key" premise tells the worker that case needs no migration when the key in fact changes.
findings.text: §36's bullet "A candidate with no model keeps its existing key, because `option_key` already returns the bare backend name for it" is not what `option_key` does: it returns the bare name only when the candidate's family equals its backend name, and otherwise returns `<family>:<backend>` (the live modelless backend `native` renders as `in-harness:native`, since `lane_family` reads its launch kind)

findings.reason: a coordinator reading the graph can dispatch §37 before §36 and build the row against a candidate table that has not yet been split, which is exactly the collapsed state §37's assertions assume away.
findings.text: the `plan-section-depends-on` meta declares no entry for `s36` or `s37`, although §37 is written "Once §36 lands", its done-when runs §36's own new test file, and its followup (line 508) says "Builds after §36"

findings.reason: the citation points a reader checking the claim at a function signature rather than at the code the section is about; it is a one-line correction, not a change of mechanism.
findings.text: §36 cites `reckon/crew/picker/lane_context.py:338` for `blocks[str(backend)]`, but line 338 is `def return_times(` and the keying line is 388, so the anchor was written against an earlier revision of the module

findings.reason: the three mutations are each stated explicitly and independently, so a worker applies all three whichever number the sentence names; only the wording is wrong.
findings.text: §37's negative control reads "two mutations, each applied alone" and then lists three, so its declared count disagrees with its own list

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §36 cites `reckon/crew/picker/lane_context.py:338` for `blocks[str(backend)]`, which is at line 388; the cited line is `def return_times(`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §37's negative control opens "two mutations, each applied alone" and then states three, so its declared count and its list disagree.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both gate on pytest over named test files and record their figures (representative_state_tokens, at base and head) in the manifest; no scratchpad or node-local path is named.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `suits`, `price` and `option_key` name what they carry and no plan label, gate id, ticket number or version tag reaches code or a symbol.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §37 reads each model's price through a per-backend map that never holds a lane's non-default models, and asserts a per-model `backends` entry that lane expansion does not create; its central mechanism cannot produce its done-when.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §36 keys two tables by one key, and §37's one deliverable is the content a model's row declares (its suit beside its price); each is closable on one verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §37 declares no `plan-section-depends-on` edge on §36 although its deliverable, done-when and followup all require §36 to have landed first.
